draft.title: Changing the subject of a formula
card: The subject of a formula is the pronumeral on its own on one side, such as \(A\) in \(A = \pi r^{2}\). Changing the subject means rearranging so a different pronumeral is on its own.
Use the same inverse steps as when solving an equation. Do the same thing to both sides, and undo the operations in the reverse order to how they were applied.
Example: make \(r\) the subject of \(A = \pi r^{2}\). Divide both sides by \(\pi\) to get \(\frac{A}{\pi} = r^{2}\). Then take the square root of both sides.
This gives \(r = \sqrt{\frac{A}{\pi}}\), taking the positive root because a radius is a length. Always divide or subtract the whole of the other side, not just part of it.
draft.remember: Undo each operation with its inverse, on both sides, until the pronumeral you want stands alone.

a.q: Make \(x\) the subject of \(y = 3x + 5\). Which is correct?
a.why: First subtract 5 from both sides to get \(y - 5 = 3x\), then divide the whole of the left side by 3. Dividing only \(y\) by 3 is tempting, but the 5 must be divided by 3 too.
a.clue: Undo the addition first, then the multiplication.

b.q: The formula \(v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as\) gives the speed of a moving object. Which is \(a\) made the subject, with \(a > 0\) not needed?
b.why: Subtract \(u^{2}\) from both sides to get \(v^{2} - u^{2} = 2as\), then divide both sides by \(2s\). Writing \(\frac{v^{2}}{2s} - u^{2}\) is tempting, but it divides only one term by \(2s\).
b.clue: Get the term with \(a\) alone first, then divide by what multiplies \(a\).

problems.detail: The phrase "with \(a > 0\) not needed" is confusing and ungrammatical. Nothing in the rearrangement involves a sign condition on \(a\), so students may wonder what it means. It should be removed.

"Always divide or subtract the whole of the other side, not just part of it" is misleading. You subtract a term from both sides; you do not subtract "the whole of the other side". The rule about the whole side only applies to dividing or multiplying, for example dividing all of \(y - 5\) by 3.

check.summary: Both intended answers are correct. Question b has a confusing phrase, "with \(a > 0\) not needed", that should be removed. The card's last line wrongly says to "subtract the whole of the other side" when only dividing applies to the whole side.
